headline: High: RD-Agent’s broad networked research defaults can leak or act on Marker-produced content, while Marker’s local document processing creates a low direct-risk but nonzero interaction surface.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Marker is local document-processing with no network egress or browser, so it can only influence RD-Agent if its outputs are manually or file-fed into RD-Agent. RD-Agent can ingest research artifacts and browse the web, but no shared channel is documented, so the injection path is unusual rather than default.
conditions: IF Marker outputs are copied into RD-Agent prompts or log files are parsed as instructions
IF an operator enables a shared filesystem bridge between the two agents
mitigations: Keep Marker outputs in a separate folder from RD-Agent inputs
Disable any prompt ingestion from files unless explicitly reviewed
Use a one-way export format with instruction stripping
Add a manual review step before RD-Agent consumes Marker text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Marker has no filesystem read/write or network egress, so it is unlikely to leak directly. RD-Agent, however, has broad network egress and API-based data flows plus secret handling, so if Marker-produced documents contain sensitive content and are handed to RD-Agent, that content can leave the local boundary through RD-Agent’s default external calls.
conditions: IF Marker-produced documents contain sensitive data and are passed into RD-Agent
IF RD-Agent is configured to call external APIs on those documents
mitigations: Redact sensitive fields before passing documents onward
Restrict RD-Agent to non-sensitive corpora
Disable external API calls for sensitive runs
Store Marker outputs in an access-controlled directory
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately if leakage is suspected

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Marker cannot write files or modify git state, so it cannot contend for mutable resources with RD-Agent. RD-Agent can support multiple instances and writes logs, but without Marker write access there is no meaningful shared-write conflict; the remaining risk is limited to accidental log/file overlap if an operator creates one.
conditions: IF an operator manually points both agents at the same log directory
IF RD-Agent is run with additional write permissions not shown in the profile
mitigations: Use separate working directories
Keep Marker read-only in its own sandbox
Avoid sharing git repositories between the agents
Name log directories distinctly per agent

D_cascading_error.rationale: Marker can transform documents, and RD-Agent’s research workflow can treat inputs as evidence for downstream generation or automation. Because RD-Agent has browser and API access, any unverified Marker output can cascade into broader actions unless an explicit verification step is inserted; the interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF RD-Agent consumes Marker output as authoritative evidence
IF no human or programmatic verification step is inserted before RD-Agent acts
mitigations: Require source citation checks before RD-Agent acts
Insert a human review gate for Marker-derived claims
Mark Marker output as untrusted metadata
Disable downstream automation on first-pass outputs

E_compliance.rationale: Marker is a document-processing tool with no declared data classes, while RD-Agent explicitly touches financial reports, papers, competition datasets, execution traces, logs, and handles API keys. If Marker is used on regulated or sensitive documents and those are then processed by RD-Agent’s cloud-backed workflows, retention and residency obligations can diverge; the other agent is cited because the mismatch arises in the pair.
conditions: IF Marker processes regulated documents that are later sent to RD-Agent
IF RD-Agent’s external API providers retain or log those documents
mitigations: Classify documents before handing them to RD-Agent
Exclude regulated data from RD-Agent runs
Review vendor retention terms for each API used
Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workflows
